# Zstandard source repairs

These packages preserve the Zstandard format used by existing transcript spools
and negotiated HTTP requests. They are locally maintained source, not an audit
approval of the corresponding unmodified crates.io releases.

`zstd-provenance.json` records the exact published archive SHA-256, original file
hashes, and repair patch SHA-256. Original licenses, Cargo manifests, and VCS
provenance are retained. Only each archive's development `Cargo.lock` is omitted;
the consuming workspaces own dependency resolution.

The repairs cover:

- `zstd-safe` output buffers reject a starting position beyond initialized data.
  Previously, a safe call could mark an unwritten prefix of a vector initialized.
- Prepared dictionary references borrow the dictionary object for the context's
  lifetime, including the high-level streaming wrappers.
- The WebAssembly allocator checks multiplication/addition, layout validity, and
  allocation failure, preserves alignment, and accepts `free(NULL)`.
- Raw-pointer exports expose their unsafe contracts. Zero-length memory calls
  avoid dereferencing null pointers. Sort comparisons use aligned copies of
  `MaybeUninit` bytes so packed inputs and C padding are handled correctly.

Cargo consumes these source directories in the Rust, Maestro, DX, and business
integration workspaces. Bazel fetches the same checksum-pinned registry archives
and applies the matching patches. The normal Bazel Cargo projection check
reverses each patch in an isolated copy and verifies every original source hash,
the exact file inventory, Cargo paths, and Bazel annotations. Its mutation tests
reject changed sources, hashes, missing provenance, symlinks, and divergent
build configuration. This establishes source equivalence, not memory safety of
the entire dependency.

After an intentional reviewed source edit, regenerate the patches using
`python3 scripts/update-vendored-zstd-patches.py` from the Mono root. That command
requires locally cached archives matching the recorded published checksums; it
does not update upstream hashes or supply-chain approvals. Run
`make bazel-cargo-dependency-manifest-check` and
`python3 scripts/test-vendored-zstd.py` with the normal shared Cargo target.

The focused suite covers initialized-prefix rejection and preservation,
compile-fail dictionary lifetimes, allocator overflow/null/zeroing, comparator
alignment, and the active bulk/stream codec path. `zstd-existing-transcript.hex`
was generated by the unmodified registry release using level 1 compression of
`b"existing transcript representation".repeat(4096)`; the patched encoder must
produce exactly those bytes, and the decoder must recover the original input.

Independent review compared all 95 bundled upstream files to the official
Zstandard v1.5.7 release and inspected build/provenance and active native decoder
header, window, output-capacity, and allocation checks. This is not a complete
line-by-line audit of all native code, experimental/seekable APIs, or every
target. The shim tests execute on the test host; they do not claim a WebAssembly
runtime acceptance test. Platform API retains its 8 MiB decoder-window and
1 MiB decoded-request limits. Normal cargo-vet coverage for the remaining
third-party dependency graph remains required; no exemption or trust import is
introduced by this source repair.
